1.note: דֳּמִי is "stillness, silence" (Isa 62:6, Ps 83:2). The image (joy melting in a furnace of silence) is uncertain; a sense "grief" or "blood" (דָּם) is also possible.

2.note: כַּפּוֹת can be palms of the hands or palm fronds (Lev 23:40, כַּפֹּת תְּמָרִים): trees planted by rivers. The subject is the "daughters of hope" of the line before.

3.note: הָרֹאוֹת "the eyes" as in Eccl 12:3. מַחֲרִיטֵי is read from חֶרֶט "engraving tool" (Exod 32:4): the tears cut grooves in the eyes. Uncertain.

4.he: וְהוֹרוּ חֲלוּצֵי שְׁלוֹמִי אֲשֶׁר מָגִנֵּיהֶם אֲפִיקִים
4.note: הוֹרוּ is read as "shot" (from ירה), as the next line takes up 1 Kgs 22:34, where a man shoots between the joints and the mail. Job 41:7 אֲפִיקֵי מָגִנִּים is "rows (or channels) of shields"; here אֲפִיקִים also rhymes with the streams of line 39.

5.note: Play on Prov 16:18 "before ruin (שֶׁבֶר) comes pride" and on שֵׂבֶר "hope" (Ps 146:5): the two words differ only in ש/שׂ.

6.note: The word חָמֵשׁ is in square brackets in the edition, an editor's addition. With it the phrase is Gen 43:34 "five times as much".

7.note: Letter play: פלד "steel" and דלף "dripping" share the same letters in a new order. The eyes, dried of tears, become hard as steel.

8.note: Exod 38:8: the laver made from "the mirrors of the women who served" at the Tent of Meeting. The sense here is unclear: perhaps the troubles that stood like a reflection before him.

9.note: Play on לֶקַח "teaching" and לָקְחוּ "they took". וַיָּשׂלוּ is read as "drew out" (perhaps from נשל, to draw or slip off); uncertain.

10.note: Pun on עֲנָק: "necklace" (Prov 1:9) in one line, and the giant sons of Anak with the Nephilim (Num 13:33) in the next. צְנִינִים are the "thorns" of Num 33:55.

11.note: Job 37:2. The edition's full stop falls after מְקוֹרוֹת, so "in the utterance that goes out of his mouth" stands in this line with what follows; the sense joins it to the binding of the line before.

12.note: שְׁאָט is "scorn" (Ezek 25:6). The sense "at their scorn" is uncertain; it may mean the force of their onset, paired with "their stamping" in the next line.

13.note: In Job 39:13 כְּנַף רְנָנִים is "the wing of the ostrich"; here רְנָנִים is taken in its sense "songs". The same play returns in line 161.

14.note: אֲלֻמִּים are "sheaves" (Gen 37:7); מְסִבָּה is a circle or company at table. The phrase, perhaps the gathered company of higher beings, is unclear.

15.note: הוֹיוֹת is unclear: perhaps "existing, holding" (from היה/הוה), or a philosophical term for "beings".

16.note: סַף is a threshold or a basin; the sense here (other speech is barren, without this tree) is uncertain.

17.note: Pun: חֲרָבוֹת "swords" and חֳרָבוֹת/חֲרֵבוֹת "waste places", with the same consonants.

18.note: Num 11:2 "and the fire sank down". Here the sea, dried up, sinks down upon the fire; the construction is difficult.

19.note: Ps 32:9 "whose trappings (עֶדְיוֹ) must be curbed (לִבְלוֹם) with bit and bridle". In Hebrew the six verdicts rhyme on the poems' rhyme words: יִבְלֹם, יִגְלֹם, יַהֲלֹם, and so on. The sense of each verdict is not always clear.

20.note: עֵילוֹם is a spelling of עוֹלָם "world, eternity", chosen for the rhyme with חֲלוֹם and שָׁלוֹם.
